name: Quan Khanh Luu
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: Tactile representation learning connects directly to embodied manipulation: TacImag predicts useful contact representations from vision and proprioception, while tactile-aware loco-manipulation combines imitation learning and reinforcement learning on mobile hardware.

physicalEvidence.summary: July 2026 TacImag reports a real Franka Panda with front/wrist RealSense D415 cameras. GelSight records paired training demonstrations, but is replaced by a geometrically matched dummy finger during deployment. Diffusion policies are evaluated over 15 trials per configuration on bulb installation, wiping, belt insertion and ball sorting. April 2026 tactile-aware loco-manipulation additionally uses a real Unitree Go2 with D1 arm and FlexiTac sensor array.

shortVisit.summary: No dedicated external visiting-student or short-term internship invitation was found on the directly inspected homepage. A public professional email is available, but availability is unknown and receives zero short-visit points.

unknowns: The verified 2026 hardware papers identify Luu with Purdue, preceding the new UNL appointment; current UNL lab equipment, access and visitor-hosting readiness are not established. TacImag hardware is corroborated collaboration, not evidence that the new UNL lab owns that Panda. Its reported contact-task gain is 44.4 percentage points, not relative percent; fixed task fixtures and viewpoint sensitivity limit generalization. ManiFeel on the homepage is explicitly a simulation benchmark and is not used as physical robot evidence.

Summer 2027 acceptance, mentor capacity, exact dates, funding, visitor appointment, and applicable university/immigration approvals remain unconfirmed. Self-funding alone does not establish eligibility.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
